opening_message:
Ticket 1: Jesse Stewart (employee ID E013) requests admin access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E013.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Payroll: admin
  - comment: Jesse Stewart (E013) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role, so admin is permitted. Recommend granting admin as requested.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Jesse Stewart (E013) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as noted earlier. Contractors can never have admin. With basic training, max access is read. Recommend granting read.
reason: Jesse Stewart (E013) requests admin access to Payroll. The Security DB note indicates Jesse is a contractor with basic security training (correcting the earlier note that listed full-time). Per policy, contractors can never have admin; with basic security training the maximum access is read. Since the requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum, grant the maximum: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Jesse Stewart (E013) requests admin access to Payroll.

Two notes in memory:
- Note 1: full_time Payroll Specialist, recommends admin (Payroll owned by Payroll Specialist, so admin permitted for full_time employee whose role owns system).
- Note 2: contractor with basic security training, recommends read. Contractors never admin. With basic training, max is read.

The notes conflict on employment type. Note 2 explicitly says the Security DB shows contractor, not full-time as noted earlier. This is a correction from a later/more authoritative source (Security). 

Per policy:
- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.
- Jesse has basic security training → max is read.
- Requested level = admin, which is above max (read). Grant maximum = read.

So decision: read.

Let me submit.
